info.name: Library API (Biblioteca Virtual)
info.description:
Every request of the Library API (FastAPI) used by the Biblioteca Virtual frontend.

**Setup**
1. Import this collection and `library-api.local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the *Library API - local* environment.
3. If the backend `.env` sets `API_KEY`, paste the same value into the environment's `apiKey`. Leave it empty when the API has no key.
4. Run folder 2 before 4, 5 and 6 (they need data and the saved `bookId`).

Authentication is configured once on the collection (API key in the `X-API-Key` header); requests that must not send it override it with *No Auth*.

item.name: 1. Health & docs
item.description: Operational endpoints. `/health` is public (no API key) and never rate limited.

request.description: Returns `{"status": "ok"}` when the API is up.
Machine-readable API description. Returns 404 when `ENABLE_DOCS=false`.
Interactive documentation (HTML). Open it in a browser for the best view.

item.name: 2. Register books (POST /books)
item.description: Successful registrations. The first request stores the new id in the `bookId` collection variable, used by the 'Get by id' requests.

request.description: `created_at` is omitted, so the API fills it with the current UTC date and time.
`created_at` sent in São Paulo time (-03:00) is stored and returned in UTC (`14:30:00Z`).

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone",
  "author": "J. K. Rowling",
  "publication_date": "1997-06-26",
  "summary": "A young wizard discovers his magical heritage.",
  "created_at": "2024-05-10T11:30:00-03:00"
}

request.description: A `created_at` without timezone is treated as UTC.
Only the required fields; `summary` defaults to an empty string.

item.name: 3. Validation errors (422)
item.description: Invalid payloads. Every one returns `422` with FastAPI's `{"detail": [{"loc", "msg", "type"}]}` format.

request.description: `title` is required.
Whitespace-only text is stripped and rejected as empty.
Dates must be ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; `26/06/1997` is rejected.
The pre-request script sets `{{tomorrow}}` to tomorrow's date.
The pre-request script sets `{{inOneHour}}` to one hour from now (UTC).

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Dune",
  "author": "Frank Herbert",
  "publication_date": "1965-08-01",
  "summary": "A noble family becomes embroiled in a war for control of the desert planet Arrakis.",
  "created_at": "{{inOneHour}}"
}

request.description: Unknown fields are rejected, so clients cannot set server-controlled values such as `id`.

body.raw:
{
  "id": 999,
  "title": "Dune",
  "author": "Frank Herbert",
  "publication_date": "1965-08-01",
  "summary": "A noble family becomes embroiled in a war for control of the desert planet Arrakis."
}

request.description: `summary` accepts up to 5000 characters. The pre-request script builds a 5001-character text.

item.name: 4. Search books (GET /books)
item.description: Partial, case-insensitive search by `title` and/or `author`, paginated with `skip` and `limit` (default 20, max `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` = 100). Run folder 2 first so there is data.

request.description: No filters: returns every book (first page), ordered by id.
`harry` matches *Harry Potter...*.
Case does not matter.
Both filters must match.
Skips the first book and returns at most two.
No match returns `200` with an empty list.
`%` (sent URL-encoded as `%25`) is matched literally, not as a SQL wildcard.
`limit` above `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` returns 422.
`skip` must be >= 0.

item.name: 5. Get book by id (GET /books/{book_id})
item.description: Uses the `bookId` variable saved by 'Create book (created_at omitted)'.

request.description: Returns the book registered in folder 2.
Unknown ids return `404 {"detail": "Book with id 999999 not found"}`.
Ids start at 1.
Ids must be integers.

item.name: 6. Edit & delete (PATCH / DELETE /books/{book_id})
item.description:
Not required by the assignment (which asks only for registering and searching), but included to make the API a complete CRUD.

Edits use the `bookId` saved in folder 2. Deletion first registers its own book (saved as `deleteBookId`) so the other folders keep their data.

request.description: Only the fields sent change; the others keep their value.
Datetimes with a timezone are stored and returned in UTC.
The same rules as registration apply.
`null` is rejected: omit a field to keep it unchanged.
Future dates are rejected.
The id cannot be changed; unknown fields are rejected.
Unknown ids return 404.
Registers a throwaway book and saves its id as `deleteBookId`.
Deletes the book; the response has no body.
After deletion, the id is no longer found.
Deleting a missing book returns 404.

item.name: 7. Security
item.description: Requests that exercise the security layer (see the Security section of the README). The API key tests only apply when the server sets `API_KEY`.

request.description: No `X-API-Key` header. Returns 401 when the server has `API_KEY` set (200 otherwise).

exec: pm.test("401 when the API requires a key", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([401, 200]));

request.description: An incorrect key. Returns 401 when the server has `API_KEY` set.

exec: pm.test("401 when the API requires a key", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([401, 200]));

request.description: Bodies above `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` (64 KB by default) are rejected before parsing. The pre-request script builds a ~70 KB summary.
A browser preflight from an origin listed in `CORS_ORIGINS`.
Origins outside `CORS_ORIGINS` get no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, so browsers block the response.
Hosts outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS` get 400. The request overrides the `Host` header with `evil.example`; if your Postman version does not send custom `Host` values, the API answers 200 instead.

exec: pm.test("400 (if Postman sent the custom Host)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([400, 200]));

request.description: Every response carries defensive headers; `/books` responses also show the remaining rate-limit budget. Run this request many times (e.g. Collection Runner, 301 iterations) to see `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`.
